model.name: Dependency / Impact
model.purpose: Supply the criticality, impact-estimation and resilience-posture layer of the Dependency / Impact mixin: how important a declared dependency is to a named dependent purpose, what a loss of it would cost, how likely and how well-evidenced that estimate is, and which substitution, redundancy, correlated-failure and concentration conditions qualify it - always as scheme-qualified assertions attached to dependency facts owned elsewhere.
model.scope_statement: This is the criticality and resilience slice of WM-XCT-037. It models judgements about dependencies: criticality assignment, scale-scheme binding, downstream impact projection, affected-set (blast radius) snapshots, likelihood and estimate qualification, substitutes, redundancy and correlated failure, single points of failure and concentration, and references to externally owned mitigations. It excludes the typed dependency edge and graph topology (the adjacent split area of the same model) and all host-owned risk, continuity, control and incident records. Estimates stay separate from dependency facts: an edge asserts that a relation exists; a criticality or impact record asserts a judgement about that relation under a named scheme, authority and validity window.
in_scope: Criticality assignment of a depended-on element relative to a named dependent purpose, operating state and time window
Binding of every stored criticality, severity or likelihood value to a published scheme identifier and version instead of an embedded universal scoring doctrine
Downstream impact estimation per consequence category and per assumed loss scenario, including sensitivity to disruption duration
Affected-set (blast radius) snapshots derived by declared traversal rules over a referenced dependency-graph snapshot
Likelihood, confidence, evidence sufficiency and residual uncertainty attached to each estimate
Declared substitutes and alternates with switchover conditions, qualification evidence and capacity limits
Redundancy configuration, effective independence and correlated or common-cause failure conditions
Derived single-point-of-failure determinations and concentration exposure at element, supplier, jurisdiction or facility level
Outbound references to mitigations, controls and continuity objectives, with credited effect and residual values
out_of_scope: Typed dependency edges, direction, dependency kinds and graph topology - owned by the adjacent dependency-fact split of WM-XCT-037
Risk evaluation, risk acceptance, risk appetite and treatment decisions - owned by the host risk register model
Creation, approval, execution, effectiveness testing and audit trail of any mitigation or control
Business continuity planning and the setting of impact tolerances, MTD, RTO, RPO or MBCO values
Runtime failover, orchestration, remediation or any enforcement action
Incident detection, incident lifecycle and post-incident review records
Definition or publication of scoring schemes themselves (CVSS, SSVC, FMECA RPN, sector scales) - bound by reference only
Asset, service and supplier master data and their lifecycle
Vulnerability discovery, exploit intelligence and patch management

boundary_notes.neighbor: Dependency-fact core of WM-XCT-037 (adjacent split area)
boundary_notes.distinction: That part owns edge identity, dependency type, direction and graph snapshots. This part attaches criticality and resilience judgements to those edges and stores no topology of its own; an affected-set snapshot cites a graph snapshot rather than reproducing it.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Host risk register and risk assessment model
boundary_notes.distinction: NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 places likelihood, impact and risk determination inside a risk assessment process. This model supplies dependency-specific impact and likelihood inputs and the reference to the consuming risk record, but never asserts a risk level, acceptance decision or treatment plan.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Control, treatment and mitigation record model
boundary_notes.distinction: Mitigations are referenced with a credited effect and a residual value only. Approval, execution, effectiveness testing and audit-trail semantics remain entirely with the owning system; a reference here grants no enforcement or audit ownership.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Business continuity and operational resilience model
boundary_notes.distinction: MTD, RTO, RPO and impact tolerances are set and owned by continuity or supervisory frameworks (NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1; BCBS operational resilience principles). This model cites them as reference thresholds when expressing time-to-impact and duration sensitivity, and never authors or approves them.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Severity and criticality scale scheme publishers (FIRST CVSS, CISA SSVC, IEC FMECA)
boundary_notes.distinction: Schemes are aligned, not absorbed. CVSS v4.0 and SSVC produce non-interconvertible outputs (numeric severity band versus a Track/Attend/Act decision), so values are stored scheme-qualified and no canonical cross-scheme normalisation is asserted.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Supplier and third-party risk management (C-SCRM, DORA oversight)
boundary_notes.distinction: Supplier master data, contractual registers and regulatory designation of critical providers belong to supplier-risk and legal-register models. This model records only concentration measures and substitutability conditions computed over dependencies it already references.

sources.title: NIST IR 8179, Criticality Analysis Process Model: Prioritizing Systems and Components
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)
sources.relevance: Establishes criticality analysis as a structured method of prioritizing programs, systems and components by their importance to organizational goals and the impact of their failure; anchors criticality as a purpose-relative judgement rather than an intrinsic property.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1, Guide for Conducting Risk Assessments
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)
sources.relevance: Normative separation of likelihood of occurrence, level of impact and resulting risk across a three-tier hierarchy; source of the dependency-based definition of criticality and of qualitative/semi-quantitative assessment scales. Marks risk determination as host-owned.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 2 Rev. 1, Developing Cyber-Resilient Systems: A Systems Security Engineering Approach
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)
sources.relevance: Cyber resiliency constructs (goals, objectives, techniques, approaches, design principles) and the capability to anticipate, withstand, recover from and adapt; supplies the definition of criticality as an attribute reflecting relative importance to stated goals, and grounds redundancy and mitigation referencing.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1, Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)
sources.relevance: Source of maximum tolerable downtime ('the amount of time mission/business process can be disrupted without causing significant harm to the organization's mission') and of business impact analysis with recovery criticality, resource requirements and recovery priorities - all cited here as externally owned thresholds.

sources.title: NIST Computer Security Resource Center Glossary - entries for 'criticality' and 'impact'
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)
sources.version_or_date: Entries as published and accessed 5 September 2026, citing CNSSI 4009-2022, NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1, NIST SP 800-60 Vol. 1/2 Rev. 1, NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 2 Rev. 1 and NIST SP 800-160v1r1
sources.relevance: Documents four coexisting and non-identical definitions of criticality (consequence of incorrect behaviour, degree of mission dependence, relative importance to stated goals, degree of impact on development or operation), which is direct evidence that criticality values must be scheme-qualified.

sources.title: Common Vulnerability Scoring System v4.0 Specification Document
sources.organization: Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams (FIRST)
sources.relevance: A published severity scheme with Base/Threat/Environmental/Supplemental metric groups, an explicit vector-string notation, a None-Critical rating band and Environmental metrics that let a consumer modify severity for asset importance; also states that factors outside CVSS belong to broader risk processes.

sources.title: Stakeholder-Specific Vulnerability Categorization (SSVC)
sources.organization: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA, U.S. Department of Homeland Security)
sources.version_or_date: CISA decision tree customization published 2020; page accessed 5 September 2026
sources.relevance: A competing, non-numeric prioritisation scheme using decision points (exploitation, technical impact, automatable, mission prevalence, public well-being) and outcomes Track / Track* / Attend / Act - evidence that severity outputs are scheme-shaped and not interconvertible with numeric scores.

sources.title: National Critical Functions
sources.organization: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA, U.S. Department of Homeland Security)
sources.version_or_date: NCF set of 55 functions in four categories; page content updated through September 2020, accessed 5 September 2026
sources.relevance: Defines functions whose disruption would have a debilitating effect and frames holistic analysis of risks and associated dependencies with cascading impacts within and across sectors - primary support for propagation, cross-boundary affected sets and functional rather than entity-level criticality.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector (DORA)
sources.organization: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.relevance: Binding treatment of critical or important functions, ICT concentration risk, criticality designation criteria for third-party providers and mandatory exit strategies and transition periods - primary support for concentration exposure and substitutability being first-class, and for their designation being externally owned.

sources.title: IEC 60812:2018, Failure modes and effects analysis (FMEA and FMECA)
sources.relevance: Applies to hardware, software, processes including human action and their interfaces; states that where ranking of criticality involves at least the severity of consequences the analysis becomes FMECA, and offers alternative means of calculating risk priority numbers - evidence that severity ranking methods are plural and must be named.

sources.title: IEC 61078:2016, Reliability block diagrams
sources.relevance: Requirements for modelling system dependability with reliability block diagrams, qualitative and quantitative analysis, availability and failure-frequency calculation, and stated relationships with fault tree analysis (IEC 61025) and Markov techniques (IEC 61165) - the method basis for redundancy configuration and derived single-point-of-failure findings.

sources.title: Principles for operational resilience
sources.organization: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, Bank for International Settlements
sources.version_or_date: Consultative document, 6 August 2020 (final principles issued 31 March 2021)
sources.relevance: Principles-based supervisory framing of the ability to withstand operational risk-related events, drawing on outsourcing guidance - used to place tolerance for disruption, critical operations and third-party reliance in a host discipline outside this model.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1 Update 1, Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices for Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)
sources.version_or_date: May 2022, includes updates as of 1 November 2024 (final)
sources.relevance: Confirms cybersecurity supply chain risk management as a distinct host discipline for identifying, assessing and mitigating supply-chain risk, including risk assessments for products and services - used only to place supplier assessment and treatment outside this model's boundary.

sources.title: CycloneDX Specification Overview (standardised as ECMA-424)
sources.version_or_date: CycloneDX v1.7 released 21 October 2025; ECMA-424 published 10 December 2025
sources.relevance: An interoperable representation of components, services, dependencies and relationships in which known vulnerabilities and their exploitability are communicated - the exemplar for keeping dependency facts separate from attached severity assertions and for exchanging both under a versioned specification.

bundles.name: Criticality and impact estimation
bundles.description: Judgements about how important a dependency is and what its loss would cost, each bound to a named scheme, a declared loss scenario and an explicit qualification of likelihood and confidence.
bundles.rationale: Criticality analysis is a structured prioritisation of systems and components by their importance to organizational goals and the impact of their failure (NIST IR 8179), while NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 keeps likelihood, impact and resulting risk as separate determinations. Grouping assignment, scale binding, impact projection and estimate qualification in one bundle keeps every estimate traceable to a scheme, a scenario and an evidence basis, and keeps the risk conclusion outside the model.

layers.name: Criticality basis and scale binding
layers.description: What a criticality value means: the subject and purpose it relates, the authority that set it, and the published scheme and version under which the value is interpreted.

findings.name: Criticality assignment to a dependency
findings.description: A criticality value asserted for a depended-on element as seen from one named dependent purpose, valid for a stated operating state and time window, with the deciding authority recorded. Criticality is relational, not intrinsic: the same element may carry different values for different purposes.

questions.text: Which depended-on element and which dependent purpose does this criticality assignment bind together?
answer_data: Reference to the dependency edge in the dependency-fact core
Reference to the dependent mission, service or function

questions.text: What criticality level is asserted, and under which named scheme and version is that level defined?
answer_data: Criticality level code as published by the scheme

questions.text: Which role or body determined the level, by what method, and where is that decision recorded?
For which operating state and validity window does the assignment hold?
answer_data: Operating state or condition code (normal, degraded, surge, seasonal)

questions.text: Does the assigned level propagate to elements the subject itself depends on, and under which inheritance rule?

data_elements.name: Criticality assignment identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier of the assignment record, distinct from the identifier of the dependency edge it qualifies.

data_elements.name: Qualified dependency reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the typed dependency edge owned by the dependency-fact core that this assignment qualifies.

data_elements.name: Dependent purpose reference
data_elements.description: The mission, business process, service or national critical function from whose viewpoint criticality is judged.

data_elements.name: Scheme-qualified criticality level
data_elements.description: The asserted level expressed as a code drawn from the bound scheme, never as a free-standing number.

data_elements.name: Validity window and operating state
data_elements.description: Operating state plus valid-from/valid-to timestamps that bound the assertion in time.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A criticality assignment is a structured assertion made of references, a scheme-qualified code, an authority pointer and a validity window. It produces no medium of its own: the decision paperwork lives in the deciding body's record system and is cited, and the analysis that supports the level is captured by the impact-assessment and dependability-model artifacts declared in other findings. Materialising an artifact here would duplicate those records and invite divergence between the stored code and the cited document.

findings.name: Scale scheme binding
findings.description: The declaration that a stored criticality, severity or likelihood value belongs to a specific published scheme version, with its publisher, value space, notation and supersession status, so no single scoring doctrine is embedded as canonical.

questions.text: Which published scheme, version and notation produced the stored value?
answer_data: Notation form (numeric band, vector string, decision-tree outcome, ordinal rank)
Metric group or decision points supplied

questions.text: Who publishes and maintains the scheme, and at which authoritative location is its definition retrievable?
answer_data: Authoritative specification URL or registry entry

questions.text: May values from two different schemes be compared, and is any declared mapping between them marked lossy?
answer_data: Permitted comparison flag per scheme pair
Lossiness marker and known distortion notes

questions.text: What becomes of stored values when the bound scheme version is superseded or withdrawn?
Which scheme inputs are mandatory and which are optional or environment-specific?
answer_data: Completeness verdict for the stored value

data_elements.name: Scheme reference
data_elements.description: Versioned reference to the published scheme under which a value is interpreted.

data_elements.name: Declared value space
data_elements.description: The permitted value set or range of the scheme, including whether values are ordinal, interval or categorical.

data_elements.name: Native notation string
data_elements.description: The scheme's own notation for the recorded value, such as a vector string or a decision-tree path.

data_elements.name: Scheme version status
data_elements.description: Whether the bound scheme version is current, superseded or withdrawn at the time of reading.

artifacts.name: Published scale scheme definition
artifacts.description: The externally published definition of a rating scheme version that stored values are bound to, such as a scoring specification, a decision-tree definition or a criticality rubric.
media_or_form: Published ranking rubric or worksheet template
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the publisher's own scheme identifier and version as the authoritative master-system identifier (for example a named specification version); otherwise the governed specification URI or registry entry; otherwise a UUID minted by the adopting Dimension with the retrieval URL and content digest recorded.

layers.name: Downstream impact projection
layers.description: What a loss of the subject would do to dependents: consequence severity per category and the extent, order and boundaries of propagation.

findings.name: Downstream impact estimate
findings.description: An estimate of the consequence to a named dependent if the subject is lost or degraded, recorded per consequence category and per assumed loss scenario, with sensitivity to disruption duration. It is an input to a host risk or continuity record and is never itself a risk determination.

questions.text: Which loss scenario does the estimate assume: total loss, partial degradation, delay, or corruption of the depended-on element?
Which consequence categories are estimated, and what severity value is recorded for each?
answer_data: Consequence category codes (operational, financial, safety, legal, individuals affected, mission)
Per-category severity value and its bound scheme
Aggregation rule if a single headline value is stored

questions.text: How does the estimated consequence change as the disruption persists?
answer_data: Referenced maximum tolerable downtime or impact tolerance value and its owner

questions.text: What evidence underpins the estimated severity and how was it obtained?
answer_data: Assessment method reference (workshop, historical loss data, simulation, contractual penalty)
Quantitative unit, currency or population count where used

questions.text: Which host record consumes this estimate, and who owns the decision made from it?
answer_data: Consuming risk, continuity or supervisory record reference
Accountable owner role in the host system

data_elements.name: Assumed loss scenario
data_elements.description: The disruption assumption under which the estimate is valid; changing it invalidates the estimate.

data_elements.name: Per-category severity value
data_elements.description: Scheme-qualified severity recorded for each consequence category considered.

data_elements.name: Quantified consequence measure
data_elements.description: Optional quantitative expression of consequence with an explicit unit, such as monetary loss, service-hours lost or population affected.

data_elements.name: Duration sensitivity profile
data_elements.description: Severity values indexed by elapsed-outage bands, referencing externally owned tolerance thresholds.

data_elements.name: Consuming host record reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the risk, continuity or supervisory record that takes this estimate as input.

artifacts.name: Impact assessment record
artifacts.description: The document or dataset produced by the assessment activity that supports the stored severity values, such as a business impact analysis extract, an assessment worksheet or a signed determination.
media_or_form: Business impact analysis worksheet or extract
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the assessment platform's document identifier as the authoritative master-system identifier; otherwise a governed document IRI; otherwise a UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, always stored with a content digest and retrieval location.

findings.name: Affected set and propagation extent
findings.description: A snapshot of which dependents are reached if the subject fails, at what propagation order, across which boundaries and with what timing. It is a derived view over a referenced dependency-graph snapshot, recorded with its traversal rule and assumptions so it can be reproduced or falsified.

questions.text: Which dependents are reached by a failure of the subject, and at what propagation order is each reached?
answer_data: Affected element references with propagation order
Count of directly versus indirectly affected elements

questions.text: Which organisational, jurisdictional, network or facility boundaries does the propagation cross?
Which graph snapshot, traversal rule and depth limit produced this affected set?
answer_data: Dependency graph snapshot reference and snapshot time

questions.text: How quickly does the effect reach each tier of the affected set?
answer_data: Buffering, queueing or cache assumptions that delay propagation

questions.text: Which reachable paths were deliberately excluded from the affected set, and on what stated ground?
answer_data: Exclusion reason code (isolated, out of scope, blocked by declared substitute)

data_elements.name: Affected-set snapshot identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of one derivation run, since the affected set changes whenever the graph or traversal rule changes.

data_elements.name: Source graph snapshot reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the dependency-graph snapshot owned by the dependency-fact core over which the traversal ran.

data_elements.name: Affected element set
data_elements.description: Collection of reached elements with propagation order and path witness.

data_elements.name: Boundary crossings
data_elements.description: Boundaries traversed by the propagation, used to signal cross-organisation or cross-sector consequence.

data_elements.name: Time to impact
data_elements.description: Elapsed time before a given propagation order is affected, expressed as a duration.

findings.inline_only_rationale: An affected set is a reproducible derivation, not a document: it is fully determined by the cited graph snapshot, the traversal rule version and the depth and exclusion parameters recorded alongside it. Storing it as inline reference data keeps it regenerable and prevents a stale rendered diagram from being mistaken for the current propagation extent. Any published visualisation is a projection produced by the interface layer, and the term 'blast radius' itself has no normative definition, so no artifact class can be claimed as canonical.

layers.name: Likelihood and estimate qualification
layers.description: The epistemic layer over every criticality and impact value: how likely the assumed disruption is, how confident the assessor is, what evidence supports that confidence and what uncertainty remains.

findings.name: Likelihood, confidence and residual uncertainty
findings.description: Qualification of an estimate: the likelihood or frequency assigned to the assumed disruption over a stated horizon under a named scheme, together with asserted confidence, its evidential basis, the residual uncertainty that remains and the conditions that invalidate the estimate. Likelihood (about the world) and confidence (about the assessment) are recorded separately and never collapsed.

questions.text: What likelihood or failure frequency is assigned to the assumed disruption, over which horizon and under which likelihood scheme?
answer_data: Likelihood value with its bound scheme and version
Basis type (historical frequency, reliability model, expert judgement)

questions.text: What confidence is asserted in the estimate, and is it derived from evidence quality, assessor agreement or a stated model?
answer_data: Confidence level under a named confidence scheme
Degree of agreement among contributing assessors

questions.text: What residual uncertainty, unmodelled factor or known unknown remains after the estimate is made?
answer_data: Sensitivity notes identifying which input dominates the result

questions.text: Which change in the underlying facts marks the estimate stale and triggers reassessment?
answer_data: Invalidation trigger conditions (edge change, scheme supersession, substitute withdrawal, realised incident)

questions.text: Who produced the estimate, and were independent reviewers or dissenting judgements recorded?

data_elements.name: Scheme-qualified likelihood value
data_elements.description: Likelihood or frequency of the assumed disruption, stored with its scheme reference and horizon.

data_elements.name: Likelihood horizon
data_elements.description: Exposure period over which the likelihood value applies, without which the value is uninterpretable.

data_elements.name: Confidence level
data_elements.description: Asserted confidence in the estimate under a named confidence scheme, kept distinct from likelihood.

data_elements.name: Residual uncertainty statement
data_elements.description: Narrative record of what the estimate does not capture, including unmodelled factors and dominant sensitivities.

data_elements.name: Estimate freshness state
data_elements.description: Whether the estimate is current, due for review or stale because a declared invalidation trigger fired.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Qualification data are attributes of an estimate rather than things in their own right: they must travel inside the same record as the value they qualify, or a consumer can read a severity without its confidence and horizon. The evidence they cite is already materialised by the impact-assessment record, the dependability model and the substitution verification record, each of which is referenced here rather than copied, so declaring a separate artifact would fragment a single assertion across two objects.

bundles.name: Resilience posture of the dependency
bundles.description: The conditions that soften or sharpen a dependency: declared substitutes and their limits, redundancy and its effective independence, single points of failure, concentration exposure, and references to externally owned mitigations.
bundles.rationale: Cyber resiliency is the capability to anticipate, withstand, recover from and adapt to adverse conditions (NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 2 Rev. 1), and dependability analysis models redundancy structures and their limits (IEC 61078:2016). DORA makes substitutability, exit strategies and concentration risk binding concerns. These posture facts qualify an impact estimate but must be recorded separately from it, because a substitute that exists on paper and one that has been exercised produce very different residual exposure.

layers.name: Substitution, redundancy and correlated failure
layers.description: Declared alternatives and redundant structures behind a dependency, their capacity and qualification limits, and the shared conditions that can defeat them together.

findings.name: Declared substitute or alternate
findings.description: An alternative that can carry the dependent's need if the subject is unavailable, recorded with equivalence class, invocation preconditions, capacity and duration limits, switchover cost and the evidence that it has been verified. Declaration is not capability: unverified substitutes are marked as such.

questions.text: Which alternative element can carry the need, and is it a full, partial or degraded-mode equivalent?
answer_data: Equivalence class code (full, partial, degraded mode, manual workaround)
Functions not covered by the substitute

questions.text: Under which declared preconditions is the substitution considered available and valid?
answer_data: Precondition list (contract in force, data replicated, licence available, staff trained)
Named condition owner for each precondition

questions.text: What capacity, throughput or duration ceiling limits the substitute, and what share of demand can it absorb?
answer_data: Maximum sustainable period in substitute mode

questions.text: How long does switchover take, and what degradation or data loss is accepted while the substitute is in effect?
answer_data: Data-loss window and its referenced recovery-point objective owner

questions.text: When was the substitute last exercised or otherwise verified, and with what recorded result?
answer_data: Verification method (live failover, tabletop exercise, contractual attestation)

data_elements.name: Substitute element reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the element, supplier or manual procedure proposed as an alternative.

data_elements.name: Equivalence class
data_elements.description: How completely the substitute replaces the subject, including declared functional gaps.

data_elements.name: Capacity limit
data_elements.description: Quantified ceiling on what the substitute can carry, with an explicit unit and any time bound.

data_elements.name: Switchover duration
data_elements.description: Expected elapsed time to bring the substitute into effect, used in time-to-impact reasoning.

data_elements.name: Verification state
data_elements.description: Whether the substitute is unverified, attested, tested or proven in a real event, with the last verification time.

artifacts.name: Substitution verification record
artifacts.description: Evidence produced by one verification of a declared substitute, such as a failover test report, an exercise record or a contractual exit-plan attestation.
media_or_form: Continuity exercise record or drill log
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the identifier issued by the exercising or testing system of record as the authoritative master-system identifier; otherwise a governed IRI for the exercise programme instance; otherwise a ULID minted by the adopting Dimension. Each verification run is a distinct instance and is never identified by its date alone.

findings.name: Redundancy configuration and correlated failure
findings.description: The redundant structure standing behind a dependency, expressed as a required-out-of-total configuration with its mode, together with the shared resources, suppliers, locations or designs that reduce effective independence and can defeat the redundancy at once.

questions.text: What redundancy configuration is declared, expressed as which structure and which required-out-of-total quantity?
Which resources, suppliers, sites, code bases or time sources are shared across the redundant members?
answer_data: Sharing depth (same rack, same site, same provider, same software build)

questions.text: Which common-cause or correlated failure conditions would defeat all redundant members simultaneously?
answer_data: Common-cause condition list (power, cooling, region, certificate expiry, shared defect)
Estimated correlation strength or beta-factor style parameter
Scheme reference for the correlation measure

questions.text: Is the redundancy load-sharing, so that losing one member degrades capacity rather than preserving it?
answer_data: Capacity retained after loss of one member

questions.text: Which dependability analysis method produced or supports the configuration, and what assumptions did it declare?
answer_data: Analysis method reference (reliability block diagram, fault tree, failure modes and criticality analysis)

data_elements.name: Redundancy structure
data_elements.description: Structural form of the redundancy together with required and total member counts.

data_elements.name: Redundant member references
data_elements.description: The elements that together provide the redundancy, referenced rather than duplicated.

data_elements.name: Common-cause conditions
data_elements.description: Conditions shared by the members that can cause simultaneous failure, each with a type and description.

data_elements.name: Effective independence assessment
data_elements.description: Judgement of how independent the members really are after shared conditions are accounted for, with its scheme reference.

data_elements.name: Retained capacity on single loss
data_elements.description: Capacity still available after one member is lost, expressed with an explicit unit or share.

artifacts.name: Dependability analysis model
artifacts.description: The analysis artefact that supports a redundancy or independence claim, such as a reliability block diagram, a fault tree or a failure modes, effects and criticality analysis worksheet.
media_or_form: Reliability block diagram model file or drawing
Failure modes, effects and criticality analysis worksheet
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the engineering or dependability tool's model identifier as the authoritative master-system identifier; otherwise a governed model IRI held by the owning engineering function; otherwise a UUID minted by the adopting Dimension, recorded with model version, method standard reference and content digest.

layers.name: Single points of failure, concentration and treatment linkage
layers.description: Determinations that follow from the posture facts - where no viable alternative exists and where too much converges on one element - and the outward references to mitigations that modify them.

findings.name: Single point of failure and concentration exposure
findings.description: The derived determination that a subject is a single point of failure for a named dependent, and the measured convergence of many dependents on one element, supplier, jurisdiction or facility. Both are derivations with a recorded rule version and trace, contestable and reversible, not standing labels.

questions.text: Is the subject a single point of failure for the named dependent, and from which recorded facts was that concluded?
answer_data: Determination verdict and derivation rule version
Input records used (redundancy configuration, substitute options, capacity limits)
Determination timestamp and derivation trace reference

questions.text: How many distinct dependents converge on this element, and what share of them carry a high criticality level?
answer_data: Share of dependents at or above a named criticality level

questions.text: At which level does the concentration exist: element, product, supplier, jurisdiction or shared facility?
Which change of state would remove the single-point-of-failure determination?
answer_data: Expected clearance owner in the host system

questions.text: Which determinations are contested or overridden, by whom and on what stated ground?

data_elements.name: Single-point-of-failure verdict
data_elements.description: Derived boolean-style verdict for a subject and dependent pair, valid only with its rule version and timestamp.

data_elements.name: Derivation rule version
data_elements.description: Version of the rule that produced the verdict, so that historic determinations remain interpretable.

data_elements.name: Dependent convergence count
data_elements.description: Number of distinct dependents relying on the concentrating entity under a declared counting rule.

data_elements.name: Concentration level
data_elements.description: Level at which convergence is measured, such as element, supplier, jurisdiction or facility.

data_elements.name: Determination override
data_elements.description: Recorded contest or override of a derived determination, with authority, ground and effective period.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are derivations over records this model already holds - redundancy configuration, substitute options and capacity limits - plus a rule version and a trace. They must be recomputed whenever an input changes, so freezing them into an artifact would create a document that outlives its inputs and invites reliance on a stale determination. The supporting analysis is already materialised by the dependability model artifact and is cited, and any published concentration report is an interface projection owned by the reporting process, not a record of this model.

findings.name: Mitigation and treatment reference
findings.description: Outward pointers from a criticality or resilience record to externally owned mitigations, controls, continuity plans and treatment decisions, together with the credited effect on the local estimate and the residual value after crediting. The reference carries no ownership of the mitigation's approval, execution, testing or audit trail.

questions.text: Which external mitigation, control or continuity record is referenced, and in which owning system does it live?
answer_data: Owning system identifier and record type

questions.text: Which local estimate does the referenced mitigation modify, and is the stored value recorded before or after crediting it?
What residual criticality or impact remains once the mitigation is credited?
answer_data: Residual value with its bound scheme
Whether the residual is accepted elsewhere and by which record

questions.text: What evidence shows the mitigation was in force at the moment the estimate was asserted?
answer_data: Evidence reference from the owning system

questions.text: Who owns approval, execution and effectiveness testing of the referenced mitigation?
answer_data: Accountable owner role in the owning system
Explicit statement that this model performs none of these

data_elements.name: External mitigation reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable pointer to a mitigation, control, plan or treatment record held by another system.

data_elements.name: Credited effect
data_elements.description: The declared modification the mitigation makes to a named local estimate, with the crediting rule used.

data_elements.name: Residual value after crediting
data_elements.description: Scheme-qualified criticality or impact value remaining once the mitigation is credited.

data_elements.name: In-force window
data_elements.description: Period during which the owning system attests the mitigation was effective, used to date-bound the credit.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding is deliberately nothing but reference data. The mitigation itself, its approval record, its test evidence and its audit trail are artifacts of the owning control, continuity or supply-chain system; reproducing any of them here would duplicate a governed record, create a second version that can drift, and quietly claim ownership of enforcement and audit semantics that the boundary notes place outside this model. Only the pointer, the credited effect and the residual value are held locally.

functions.name: Record criticality assignment
functions.description: Create or supersede a criticality assignment binding a dependency edge to a dependent purpose under a named scheme, authority and validity window.
outputs: Supersession link to any prior assignment
preconditions: The referenced dependency edge resolves in the dependency-fact core
The scheme version is registered and not withdrawn
effects: Creates a new assignment version; prior versions are retained as superseded rather than overwritten
Leaves the dependency edge itself unmodified
Sets the review-due timestamp from the validity window

functions.name: Register scale scheme binding
functions.description: Register a published rating, severity or likelihood scheme version so that stored values can be interpreted and validated against its declared value space.
inputs: Declared value space and notation form
Authoritative specification URL and content digest
outputs: Validation verdict for values claiming that scheme
preconditions: The version is distinct from an already-registered version
effects: Enables scheme-qualified storage and validation of values
Marks superseded scheme versions read-only for new assertions while preserving existing values
Records any declared cross-scheme mapping as lossy unless proven otherwise

functions.name: Project downstream impact and affected set
functions.description: Derive an affected-set snapshot and its propagation order from a referenced dependency-graph snapshot under a declared traversal rule, and attach the impact estimate that applies to each reached tier.
inputs: Traversal rule identifier and depth limit
outputs: Affected-set snapshot with propagation order and path witnesses
preconditions: Read access to a dependency graph snapshot owned by the dependency-fact core
A traversal rule version is declared
effects: Records a reproducible derivation with its inputs and rule version
Makes no modification to the dependency graph and triggers no operational action
Marks prior snapshots superseded without deleting them

functions.name: Qualify estimate with likelihood and confidence
functions.description: Attach likelihood, horizon, confidence, evidential basis and residual uncertainty to an existing criticality or impact estimate, and set the conditions that will mark it stale.
preconditions: The estimate exists and is not already superseded
The likelihood and confidence schemes are registered
At least one assessor identity is supplied
effects: Stores likelihood and confidence as separate fields that cannot be collapsed into one value
Sets invalidation triggers so that later fact changes mark the estimate stale
Does not compute or assert any risk level

functions.name: Derive resilience determination
functions.description: Compute this model's own single-point-of-failure verdict and concentration measures from locally recorded substitutes, redundancy configuration, capacity limits and common-cause conditions, with a full derivation trace.
inputs: Derivation rule version and counting rule
outputs: Single-point-of-failure verdict per subject and dependent pair
Derivation trace referencing every input record
preconditions: At least one redundancy or substitute record exists for the subject
A derivation rule version is declared
Counting and deduplication rules are declared for concentration measures
effects: Writes a derived determination that is regenerated rather than patched when inputs change
Performs no failover, remediation, policy enforcement or supervisory designation
Records contests and overrides alongside the verdict rather than replacing it

functions.name: Attach mitigation reference
functions.description: Link an externally owned mitigation, control or continuity record to a local estimate, record the credited effect and compute the residual value, without touching the mitigation's own lifecycle.
inputs: Mitigation record identifier and owning system
outputs: Residual value with its bound scheme
preconditions: The mitigation record reference resolves in the owning system
The owning system and accountable owner are identified
The in-force window is expressed with explicit timestamps
effects: Creates a pointer and a credited-effect record only
Never creates, approves, executes, tests or audits the referenced mitigation
Marks the credit unverified when in-force evidence is missing or stale, reducing the estimate's confidence

composition.target: WM-XCT-037 Dependency / Impact - typed dependency edge and graph facts (adjacent split area of the same model)
composition.purpose: Every criticality, impact, substitute and redundancy record attaches to a dependency edge owned there; this part stores no edge identity, direction, dependency type or topology and cites graph snapshots rather than reproducing them.

composition.target: Host risk register and risk assessment model (ISO 31000 or NIST SP 800-30 style risk records)
composition.purpose: Carry the reference to the risk record that consumes an impact or likelihood estimate. Risk determination, appetite, acceptance and treatment decisions remain with the host; this model contributes inputs only.

composition.target: Control, treatment and mitigation record model
composition.purpose: Point to mitigations that modify a local estimate and record the credited effect and residual value. Approval, execution, effectiveness testing and audit-trail semantics stay entirely with the owning system.

composition.target: Business continuity and operational resilience model (impact tolerance, maximum tolerable downtime, recovery time and recovery point objectives)
composition.purpose: Cite externally set tolerance and recovery thresholds when expressing duration sensitivity and time-to-impact. This model neither authors, approves nor tests those objectives.

composition.target: Severity, criticality and prioritisation scheme registry (CVSS, SSVC, FMECA ranking, sector-specific scales)
composition.purpose: Bind every stored value to a published scheme version and its notation, without adopting any scheme as this model's canonical doctrine or asserting conformance to it.

composition.target: Asset, service, facility and supplier registry
composition.purpose: Resolve the identity of depended-on elements, suppliers, jurisdictions and facilities used in substitution and concentration measures. Master data and its lifecycle stay in the registry.
Link realised disruptions back to the estimates that preceded them so estimates can be calibrated and marked stale. Incident detection, response and closure remain outside this model.

composition.target: Dependability analysis method alignment (failure modes and criticality analysis, reliability block diagrams, fault trees)
composition.purpose: Record which published analysis method and model version produced a redundancy, independence or single-point-of-failure claim, so the claim can be reproduced or challenged on the method's own terms.

owner_package_requirements: Name an accountable owner for scheme selection who decides which criticality, severity and likelihood schemes may be bound, and who must publish the reason when more than one scheme is permitted for the same value type.

Declare, before first use, which external systems own risk determination, mitigation execution, continuity objectives and incident records, and record their identifiers so every outbound reference resolves.

Publish and version the derivation rules for affected sets, single-point-of-failure verdicts and concentration measures, and retain superseded rule versions so historic determinations remain interpretable.
Set the maximum age after which an unqualified or unreviewed estimate is automatically marked stale, and name the role accountable for reassessment.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Prefix all local identifiers with the model slug and keep them free of dates and scheme names, so that rebinding a value to a new scheme version never forces an identifier change. Externally governed identifiers (scheme versions, mitigation records, asset references) are stored in their publisher's namespace verbatim and are never rewritten into the local namespace.
registry_links: Vercy registry entry vr.wm-xct-037 for this model and its adjacent dependency-fact split
A scheme registry entry per bound rating scheme, holding publisher, version, value space and supersession status
The adopting Dimension's system-of-record catalogue, mapping each outbound reference type to its owning system

canonicalization_rules: Sort collections by their stable local identifier, never by score, severity or recency, so canonical form does not change when values are re-estimated.
Store every criticality, severity, likelihood and confidence value together with its scheme reference and version; a bare value with no scheme binding is invalid and must not be canonicalised.
Never normalise values across schemes during canonicalisation; declared cross-scheme mappings are stored as separate, explicitly lossy annotations.
Normalise all timestamps to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset before hashing, without collapsing event time into observation time.
patch_rules: Estimates are versioned by supersession: a changed value creates a new version linked to its predecessor with a reason code, and the predecessor is never edited in place.

Derived records - affected sets, single-point-of-failure verdicts and concentration measures - are regenerated from their inputs and rule version rather than patched; a patch to a derived record is rejected.
A correction that changes the meaning of a stored value (different scheme, different loss scenario, different horizon) must be issued as a new record, not as a field update.
Any patch that changes an input to a derived determination marks all dependent derivations stale in the same transaction.
compatibility_rules: Adding a new scheme binding, consequence category or substitute option is a backward-compatible minor change.
Changing the semantics of an existing scheme binding, a derivation rule or a counting rule is breaking and requires a new rule version plus retention of the old one.
Removing a required field, or making an optional qualification field required, is breaking and must be announced before consumers are cut over.
Consumers must reject records whose bound scheme version they do not recognise rather than substituting a default scheme.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the artifact - the assessment platform's document identifier, the exercising system's run identifier, the engineering tool's model identifier, or the scheme publisher's own scheme and version identifier.
Governed global identifier or IRI where no master system exists - for example the publisher's versioned specification URI or a registry entry maintained by a recognised authority.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only when neither of the above exists, and always stored together with the retrieval location and content digest.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds precision and an explicit UTC offset or the literal Z; local wall-clock strings without an offset are invalid. Event time (when the disruption occurred, when a failover exercise ran, when a mitigation came into force, when a scheme version was published) is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time (when the estimate was asserted, when the derivation ran, when the record was loaded), and neither is derived from the other. Where the two differ materially the record carries both, and freshness and staleness decisions are computed from observation time while duration sensitivity is computed from event time.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serially produced artifacts - each failover test, exercise or verification run - are identified by the producing system's run identifier combined with the RFC 3339 start timestamp of the run, never by a date or a sequence label alone. A human-readable title may be attached for display but is never the identifier, and re-running a verification always creates a new instance rather than updating the previous one.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact reference carries a content digest (algorithm and value) alongside its retrieval location and the time the digest was computed. If the digest cannot be computed or no longer matches, the reference is marked unverified and every estimate citing it inherits a reduced confidence level and is flagged for review; unverified artifacts are never silently treated as evidence.

policies: No stored criticality, severity, likelihood or confidence value may exist without a bound scheme identifier and version; this model embeds no default scoring doctrine of its own.
Impact and likelihood estimates are inputs, not risk determinations: this model never asserts a risk level, a risk acceptance, a remediation obligation or a supervisory designation.

Declared resilience is distinguished from verified resilience: substitutes and redundancy that have not been exercised or attested are recorded as unverified and reduce the confidence of any estimate that credits them.
Derived determinations must carry their rule version and a trace to every input record, and must be reproducible from those inputs alone.

Referencing a mitigation, control, continuity objective or incident record grants no ownership of its lifecycle, execution, enforcement or audit trail; such references are read-only pointers with a locally recorded credited effect.

read: Read of a criticality or impact estimate always returns its scheme binding, validity window, freshness state and confidence together with the value; partial projections that strip qualification are prohibited for machine consumers.
Derived records are readable together with their rule version and derivation trace, and are marked stale when any input has changed since derivation.
Historic superseded versions remain readable for the retention period so that past determinations can be reconstructed as they stood.
create: Creating an estimate requires a resolvable dependency edge reference, a bound scheme version, a declared loss scenario or operating state, an assessor identity and an assertion timestamp.
Creating a substitute or redundancy record requires the referenced elements to resolve in the asset or supplier registry and requires an explicit verification state, defaulting to unverified.
Creating a mitigation reference requires the owning system identifier and the accountable owner role in that system.
update: Values are not edited in place: an update creates a superseding version with a reason code, the changed fields and the identity of the person or process making the change.
Updating an input to a derived determination marks all dependent derivations stale within the same transaction; the derivations are then regenerated rather than edited.
Scheme bindings may be updated only to record supersession or withdrawal status; the value space of a published version is immutable locally.
delete: This model's own records are retained by default and are not hard-deleted on request: superseding an estimate marks the prior version superseded and retains it for the retention period set by the adopting Dimension, with a documented default of retaining superseded assessment versions for at least the life of the dependency plus one full review cycle.

Withdrawal of a record is expressed as a tombstone carrying the record identifier, withdrawal reason, withdrawing authority and RFC 3339 withdrawal timestamp; the tombstone persists after the payload is purged so that dangling inbound references resolve to an explicit withdrawal rather than to nothing.

Purge of the payload behind a tombstone, and any legal-hold or erasure obligation, is executed under the adopting Dimension's records-retention and data-protection policy, which owns the schedule, the lawful basis and the execution; this model neither owns nor performs deletion of records held in referenced systems.

Deletion of a referenced mitigation, incident, risk or asset record is entirely owned by that record's system; this model only marks its local reference unresolved and reduces the confidence of estimates that depended on it, and never propagates a delete outward.
Artifacts held by external systems of record are never deleted through this model; only the local reference, digest and cached metadata may be withdrawn, and the withdrawal is logged.

roles.name: Model steward
responsibilities: Own the boundary against risk, continuity, control and incident models and reject local modelling of target-owned concepts
Approve derivation rule versions and their retention
Maintain the mapping from outbound reference types to owning systems

roles.name: Criticality assessor
responsibilities: Assert criticality and impact values under a bound scheme with a declared loss scenario and validity window
Record evidence, assumptions and residual uncertainty for each estimate
Raise reassessment when an invalidation trigger fires

roles.name: Dependability analyst
responsibilities: Maintain redundancy configurations, effective independence assessments and common-cause condition lists
Produce and version the dependability analysis models that support single-point-of-failure claims
Declare method assumptions and limitations alongside every model

roles.name: Scheme registrar
responsibilities: Register, version and retire bound rating schemes and record their supersession status
Reject unversioned or unattributed schemes and mark any cross-scheme mapping as lossy
Notify consumers when a bound scheme version is withdrawn

roles.name: Independent reviewer
responsibilities: Review estimates for evidence sufficiency and confidence justification
Record dissent, contests and overrides with authority and effective period
Verify that mitigation credits cite in-force evidence before they reduce a residual value

access.default_rule: Read access is granted per scope on a need-to-know basis and defaults to deny for aggregated views; write access is limited to the role that owns the record class. Aggregated concentration measures and single-point-of-failure verdicts are treated as more sensitive than any individual record because together they map where an organisation is most easily disrupted.
exceptions: Aggregated concentration and single-point-of-failure views require an explicit elevated grant with a stated purpose and expiry, and are excluded from broad internal read roles.
Supplier-identifying concentration data may be restricted further where contracts or sector regulation limit disclosure, with the restriction recorded against the record rather than applied silently.
Externally published scheme definitions carry no access restriction and may be cached and read openly.
Break-glass read during a live disruption is permitted for named incident roles, is time-boxed, and is recorded with the invoking identity and justification.
Safety-relevant criticality determinations may be disclosed to a regulator or safety authority on request without the normal purpose limitation, under the adopting Dimension's disclosure policy.
audit_requirements: This model keeps its own change log recording who created, superseded, withdrew or overrode each record, with event time and observation time and the reason code; it does not host or own the audit trail of any referenced system.
Every elevated or break-glass read of aggregated concentration and single-point-of-failure views is logged with identity, scope, purpose and expiry.
Derivation runs are logged with rule version, input record identifiers and output identifiers so any determination can be reproduced or refuted.
Access-log retention and any onward audit reporting follow the adopting Dimension's audit policy, which owns retention periods and evidentiary handling.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md first and resolve Name, Type, Registry ID and the boundary statement before reading any record
Read the Specification URL to learn the model's scope, exclusions and boundary notes, including which concepts belong to referenced models
Read the Storage type URL to learn how records are physically projected, treating the projection as incidental to the semantics
Read the Interface URL to learn how to query records, scheme bindings and derivation traces
Read the Processes URL to learn the assertion, qualification, derivation, supersession and withdrawal processes and which of them this model does not perform
Resolve the bound scheme registry before interpreting any stored criticality, severity, likelihood or confidence value

coverage.claim: This submission covers the criticality and resilience slice of WM-XCT-037 as assigned: criticality assignment and its scheme binding, downstream impact estimation, affected-set propagation, likelihood and estimate qualification, substitutes, redundancy and correlated failure, single points of failure and concentration, and outward mitigation references. Every structural node cites at least one live source, and eleven of the fourteen sources are primary sources from eight independent organisations. Structure not supported by a primary source is marked as a gap below rather than presented as canonical. No claim of universal or complete coverage of dependency semantics is made: dependency facts, risk determination, continuity objectives, control execution and incident handling are deliberately outside this boundary.

checklist.notes: Assignment, snapshot and derivation identifiers are distinct from the dependency edge identifier; artifact identity follows master-system, governed IRI, then minted UUID or ULID. Scheme identity is the publisher's own scheme plus version.

Estimates are versioned by supersession with reason codes; freshness states and invalidation triggers are modelled; scheme versions carry current, superseded and withdrawn states. The lifecycle of referenced mitigations, risks and incidents is explicitly not modelled here.

Criticality is modelled as relational between a depended-on element and a named dependent purpose; inheritance rules, propagation order, redundancy membership and shared-resource links are all explicit. Edge topology itself remains with the adjacent dependency-fact split.

Validity windows, likelihood horizons, duration-sensitivity profiles, time-to-impact, switchover duration, in-force windows and review-due timestamps are modelled; RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset is mandated, with event time separated from observation or ingestion time.

Assessor and reviewer identity, determination method, derivation rule version, input record trace, source graph snapshot and scheme publisher are all recorded; artifacts carry content digests and retrieval locations.

Deciding authority is recorded for assignments, and each outward reference names the owning system and accountable owner. Five roles are defined, and mitigation approval, execution and testing ownership is asked as an explicit question.

Values are validated against a registered scheme value space; unqualified values are invalid; invalidation triggers and maximum estimate age drive reassessment; derived records must be reproducible from inputs and rule version alone.
Default-deny for aggregated views across all four scopes, with five exception classes including break-glass and regulator disclosure, and audit requirements limited to this model's own change log.

Superseded versions are retained for a stated default period, withdrawal uses persistent tombstones, and execution of purge, legal hold and erasure is explicitly assigned to the adopting Dimension's records-retention and data-protection policy. Deletion in referenced systems is never propagated from here.

Scheme-qualified values, native notation preservation, lossy-mapping markers and consumer rejection of unknown scheme versions are mandated; CycloneDX and ECMA-424 provide the exemplar of exchanging dependency facts separately from attached severity assertions.

No scoring doctrine is embedded. CVSS v4.0, SSVC and FMECA-style ranking are cited as coexisting, non-interconvertible schemes, and the NIST glossary's four differing definitions of criticality are used as direct evidence that values must be scheme-qualified.
Likelihood and confidence are held as separate fields that may not be collapsed, with residual uncertainty, dominant sensitivities and recorded dissent.
Common-cause conditions, effective independence, load-sharing degradation and multi-level concentration measures are modelled, with DORA and IEC 61078 as anchors.

Handled narrowly and deliberately: boundary crossings, jurisdictions and shared facilities appear only where they change propagation or concentration. No geometry, coordinates or facility master data are modelled here.

Capacity limits, quantified consequences and retained capacity require explicit units, but no unit vocabulary is bound. The adopting Dimension must reference a units registry; naming one was outside the evidence gathered for this pass.

The model holds assessments about elements and services, not personal data, except where a consequence measure counts affected individuals; that count is a quantity here and any personal data behind it stays in the owning system under its own policy.

known_omissions: No units-of-measure registry is bound for capacity, throughput or monetary consequence values, so cross-record quantitative comparison is not yet safe.

Cascading failure dynamics beyond first-order propagation - feedback loops, congestion collapse and recovery contention - are not modelled; the affected set is a reachability snapshot, not a simulation.
Cost of resilience options and any optimisation between them are excluded; the model records posture, not investment decisions.
Temporal dependency variation (a dependency that only matters during a settlement window or a seasonal peak) is only partly served by the operating-state field and deserves a fuller treatment.
No canonical calibration loop is specified for comparing realised incident impact against prior estimates, although the incident reference makes it possible.
Human and organisational dependencies (key-person risk, skills concentration) are representable but were not given dedicated structure in this pass.
conflicts: The NIST glossary records four non-identical definitions of criticality - consequence of incorrect behaviour (CNSSI 4009-2022), degree of mission dependence (SP 800-30 Rev. 1), relative importance to stated goals (SP 800-160 Vol. 2 Rev. 1) and degree of impact on development or operation (SP 800-160v1r1). No single definition is adopted; the scheme binding requirement exists because of this conflict.

CVSS v4.0 yields a numeric score and a None-to-Critical band, while CISA's SSVC yields a Track / Track* / Attend / Act decision from decision points. These outputs are not interconvertible and no mapping between them is asserted here.

Recovery terminology diverges: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 uses maximum tolerable downtime while business continuity practice under ISO 22301 uses maximum acceptable outage and maximum tolerable period of disruption. This model references whichever value the owning system holds and does not reconcile the vocabularies.

IEC 60812:2018 notes alternative means of calculating risk priority numbers, reflecting a long-standing objection to multiplying ordinal severity, occurrence and detection ranks. This model therefore never computes a composite score of its own.
'Blast radius' is widely used in practice but has no normative definition in any source consulted; it is modelled as an affected-set snapshot with an explicit traversal rule instead.
regional_assumptions: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 binds only EU financial entities; its treatment of critical or important functions, concentration risk and exit strategies is used as evidence that these concepts are real and externally designated, not as a universal obligation.

CISA National Critical Functions and SSVC are United States federal instruments; the 55-function set and the CISA decision tree are examples of externally owned classification, not defaults for other jurisdictions.

BCBS operational resilience principles apply to banking supervision; the cited page is the August 2020 consultative document, with final principles issued in March 2021, and the adopting Dimension must confirm the applicable version.
NIST publications are United States federal guidance; adopting Dimensions in other jurisdictions should bind equivalent national or sector schemes rather than assume NIST scales apply.
Retention defaults stated in the deletion rules are placeholders subject to the adopting Dimension's jurisdictional records-retention and data-protection law.
adversarial_checks: Boundary sweep against every composition link: no bundle, layer, finding or function asserts a risk level, approves or executes a mitigation, sets or tests a continuity objective, performs failover, enforces policy, or hosts a referenced system's audit trail. The mitigation finding is deliberately reference-only with an explicit ownership question, and derive-resilience-determination states that it performs no failover, remediation, enforcement or supervisory designation.

Counterexample test for scheme neutrality: SSVC was chosen specifically because its output shape defeats any assumption that severity is numeric, and the four conflicting NIST definitions of criticality were used to falsify the idea of one canonical criticality scale. Any structure implying a single universal score was rejected.

Fact-versus-estimate separation test: dependency edges, graph snapshots, asset identity and supplier master data are all held by reference only. Affected sets cite a graph snapshot rather than embedding topology, and no finding stores an edge attribute.

Artifact discipline test: every finding was checked to carry either artifacts with a null rationale or an empty artifact array with a substantive rationale. Four findings declare artifacts that genuinely exist as media in other systems (published scheme definitions, assessment records, verification runs, dependability models); five are inline because they are assertions or reproducible derivations.

Stale-derivation attack: a determination that stays true after its inputs change is the main failure mode of this model. Patch rules forbid patching derived records, mark dependents stale in the same transaction, and require rule versions and traces so an old verdict can never be read as current.

Evidence-inflation check: unverified substitutes, missing in-force evidence and unverifiable artifact digests all reduce recorded confidence rather than being silently treated as adequate, so declared resilience cannot be mistaken for demonstrated resilience.
